coverage: Angle named categories rather than URLs, so the roster was read as four groups. Hobb's own craft essays, interviews and blog: FETCHED, 16 items (OF Blog 2003, Locus 1998 and 2005, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist 2005, SFFWorld 2005, A Dribble of Ink 2007, Fantasy Book Critic 2008, Lightspeed/Geek's Guide 2012, Writing Excuses 11.Bonus-01 2016 fan transcript, Paw Print 2020, robinhobb.com "As You Intend To Be" 2020, "What Works For Me" 2022 and "How to Write a Book" 2022, Syl R. Martin 2023, Dragonsteel 2024, LisiPieces 2025, plus "The Fan Fiction Rant" recovered from Wayback after removal from the live site). Critics and close readers on register and pacing: FETCHED (Geoffrey B. Elliott's chapter-by-chapter reread entries 1 and 226, four Vacuous Wastrel reviews, The Idle Woman, Lisa Goldstein in Strange Horizons, and Matthew Oliver's Mythlore article reached by bibliography chasing through Elliott's Fedwren Project). Craft essays and writing-advice pieces by novelists and craft sites: FETCHED (M Harold Page in Black Gate 2016, Jeffrey Outcalt's Substack epigraph essay 2024, Christopher Luke Dean at Writers Write 2020). Editors: FETCHED (Anne Groell, Hobb's Random House editor, interviewed by Julie Crisp 2016, though she discusses her own editing method rather than Hobb's prose, and both her claims are marked accordingly). Game designers: NOT FOUND as a substantive category — four targeted searches surfaced only wikis, an EN World recommendation thread and generic DM advice; the nearest thing is an unsigned, apparently machine-compiled article on rpgstorytellers.com, logged with three claims at low confidence and flagged for possible deletion. BLOCKED and recovered: aidanmoher.com refused WebFetch with HTTP 403 and yielded to curl with a browser user agent; the Mythlore PDF refused a direct fetch with HTTP 403 and was recovered from a Wayback raw capture and parsed with pdfminer; fanlore.org returned HTTP 403 and was bypassed by going to the primary via the Wayback CDX API. Substantive sources per route: named-roster and direct search 22; bibliography chasing 3; lateral search 5. WebFetch underpins no claim — it returns summaries rather than page text and once mis-attributed a page, so every source was read raw via curl with a browser user agent, stripped to text locally, and every quotation string-searched against that text by a build script that fails closed on a miss or a quotation over twelve words. 35 sources logged, 30 substantive, 127 claims. Raw captures and the claim source live in sweep/hobbcraft/; notes in sweep/find-hobb-craft.md; the record in sweep/found-hobb-craft.json.
